audit.whatIsWrong: Depth Charge is described twice as "point-and-click unstoppable" / "unstoppable and reliable".
audit.why: Unstoppable is a specific League status — immunity to displacement and crowd control. Depth Charge grants nothing of the kind: it is a target-locked shockwave that travels to its victim, knocking up anyone it passes on the way. Calling it Unstoppable tells a Zac player his own knockups will fail against a channelling Nautilus, which is a different and wrong lesson. The accurate word is undodgeable, because it tracks the target rather than being immune to anything.
audit.corrected: Depth Charge is target-locked and undodgeable at 825 range — not Unstoppable.

audit.whatIsWrong: The lane's defining number — that Nautilus hooks from further than Zac can reach — was never stated.
audit.why: Dredge Line is 1150 range against Stretching Strikes at 800. He gets a free 350-unit band in which he can open and Zac cannot answer, which is the mechanical reason the early levels are one-sided and why the correct play is to concede rather than to space better. _missing-interactions.json flags this pairing as knockup-enabler: both sides carry displacement and whoever lands it first owns the trade — with a 350-unit head start, that is him.
audit.corrected: Dredge Line 1150 vs your Q at 800.

audit.whatIsWrong: Titan's Wrath was written as something to trade around, and Dredge Line was called "his only engage".
audit.why: Titan's Wrath is a flat 12s at every rank, so it is available for essentially every early trade — it is not a window, it is a constant, and telling the player to wait it out sends them to a window that never opens. The real window is Dredge Line at 14/13/12/11/10s. Depth Charge is also engage, so "only engage" is wrong on its own terms.
audit.corrected: Bait Dredge Line (14s at rank 1) — that is the window. Titan's Wrath is flat 12s and always there.

audit.whatIsWrong: The passive was described vaguely as an "auto-root" that "chains onto your combo".
audit.why: Staggering Blow roots on Nautilus's FIRST attack against a given target. That is a per-target trigger, not a chain — it means his opening auto always lands a root and there is nothing to dodge, which is exactly why his opener is guaranteed and yours is not.
audit.corrected: His passive roots on his first auto against you.

audit.why: Riptide at 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s is his repeatable poke and wave tool; adding the number gives the player something to count between hooks.

Content win[] reads Nautilus x5, Skill, Zac against 50.46% over 432 games — the largest sample in the slice and a genuinely even record. Nautilus owning the early game and Zac taking the last stage matches both the data and the kits.

Expect that class of false positive wherever an ability name is preceded by a short word.
